sources.note: Full 2027 Application Guidelines for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation): fields, preparatory year, direct placement, qualifications, period, benefits, suspension, selection, documents, notes. Read in full (10 pages).
Call page for 2027 undergraduate embassy route: recruitment and first-screening timing, where to submit, document forms, nationality differences.

summary: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for undergraduate students on the Embassy Recommendation route lets international students study for a bachelor's degree at a Japanese national university. It is run by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, and applicants apply through the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country of nationality. The award gives a monthly allowance, waived university fees and economy-class air tickets. The scholarship period normally includes a one-year preparatory course in Japanese and other subjects.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality: you must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. Japanese nationals are not eligible. A dual national who holds Japanese nationality and lives outside Japan may apply if they choose the other nationality and give up Japanese nationality by the date of arrival in Japan; the first screening is then held at the Japanese mission of the country whose citizenship they choose.

Age: in principle you must have been born on or after 2 April 2002. Applicants who meet the academic background rule must be at least 18 at the time of admission to a Japanese university. Exceptions are only for situations in the applicant's country, such as military service duty or loss of schooling due to war. Personal reasons such as money, family, health or work are not accepted as reasons for an exception.

Academic background (any one of these): 12 years of schooling completed outside Japan (or completed by March 2027); completion of a school equal to a Japanese upper secondary school outside Japan (by March 2027); a pass in a qualification exam showing the same level as 12 years of schooling (by March 2027); or already eligible to enter a Japanese university at the time of application. For direct placement starting in the autumn term, 12 years of schooling must be expected to be complete by August 2027.

Japanese language: you must be willing to learn Japanese, be interested in Japan, and in principle be willing to study in Japanese.

Health: you must submit a health certificate on the prescribed form, signed by a physician, saying you have no physical or mental condition that would hinder study in Japan. If your health changes after submitting it, tell the Japanese mission promptly. Applicants who test positive for infectious diseases such as tuberculosis must be treated before arrival, and arrival is not approved until fully recovered.

Arrival and visa: in principle you must be able to arrive in Japan between 1 April and 7 April 2027 and not leave home before 1 April 2027. For autumn-term direct placement, arrival is within the period set by the university, normally within two weeks before or after the term start. You must newly obtain a Student visa at the Japanese mission in your country or region of nationality, even if you already hold another residence status.

Not eligible: military personnel or military civilian employees; people who cannot arrive within the specified period; previous MEXT scholarship holders (including those who withdrew after getting student status; the Honors Scholarship for privately financed students does not count as a MEXT scholarship); people also applying to another MEXT programme (including programmes starting in FY2026 or FY2027); people already enrolled or planning to enrol in Japan on a Student status as a privately financed student between application and the start of payments (with an exception if they will verifiably finish before payments start); people planning to receive another Japanese government or government-related scholarship after payments start; expected graduates who cannot meet the academic background rule by the deadline; dual nationals who cannot show they will give up Japanese nationality; people who change to a non-Student residence status after arrival; people planning long-term research, internship or leave away from the school; and anyone found cheating in the written exam of the first screening.

Other: grantees are expected to take part in school and community activities, to keep in touch with their university after graduation, and to cooperate with surveys and events run by the Japanese mission after they return home. Receiving a scholarship from a non-Japanese-government organisation is in principle allowed, but applicants should ask the Japanese mission first because some funds cannot be paid together.
age_experience_notes: Born on or after 2 April 2002 in principle; at least 18 years old at admission to a Japanese university for applicants who meet the academic background rule. Exceptions only for circumstances in the applicant's country (for example military service or war). The guidelines state no work experience requirement.
funding_summary: The guidelines list: a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000 (plus JPY 2,000 or 3,000 a month in specially designated regions, amount may change each fiscal year); waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the university; an economy-class air ticket to Japan and a return ticket at the end of the scholarship period. Accommodation, domestic travel to the home airport, airport fees, baggage and travel insurance are paid by the grantee. The scholarship lasts 5 years (April 2027 to March 2032) including the one-year preparatory course, or 7 years (to March 2034) for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course. With direct placement it lasts 4 years, or 6 years for those same fields. Payment is suspended during long absences.
programmes_note: Applicants choose a Field of Study (Social Sciences and Humanities, or Natural Sciences), a Course and up to three majors, as a first, second and third choice. In Natural Sciences, majors must come from the same course (A, B or C), except that someone who puts Natural Sciences C first may choose second and third majors from Natural Sciences B or C (C has only two majors, Medicine and Dentistry). Fields of art, including music, are not eligible. Applicants who choose 'Others' under Social Sciences and Humanities A may find it hard to find a university that accepts them. A grantee cannot change course (A, B or C) later and cannot transfer to another university.
institutions_note: Study is at a Japanese national university. MEXT decides the university after talking with the university and the preparatory institution, taking into account the first-screening exam results, results at the preparatory institution, the chosen major, the university's capacity and its region. The grantee cannot object to the decision. The preparatory year is as a rule at ABK College (Social Sciences and Humanities students) or Osaka University (Natural Sciences students). Direct placement applicants pick from a list of universities and departments supplied by the Japanese mission in their country; the guidelines do not list universities.

summary.detail: Bachelor's degree at a Japanese national university. Scholarship period 5 years including a one-year intensive preparatory course (Japanese language, plus Japanese affairs, mathematics, English and social studies for Social Sciences and Humanities students, or physics, chemistry and biology for Natural Sciences students), then the university entrance exam set by each university. Direct placement skips the preparatory year: 4 years (6 for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or six-year pharmacy). With the preparatory year, those same fields run 7 years. Classes are in Japanese except at universities that need no Japanese under direct placement. The academic year runs from 1 April to 31 March. A grantee who cannot finish the preparatory course, or cannot enter the university after it, loses the scholarship and must return home. Graduates with outstanding results who enter a master's or doctoral (first phase) course may have the period extended after an examination by MEXT.

benefits.limit_text: JPY 117,000 per month; an extra JPY 2,000 or 3,000 per month for grantees in specially designated regions
benefits.conditions: The amount may change each fiscal year because of the government budget. Payment is suspended for any long absence from the university or preparatory institution. The first payment comes one to one and a half months after arrival, into a Japan Post Bank account opened by the grantee; the guidelines suggest bringing about US$2,000 for the first weeks.

benefits.limit_text: Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the university are waived
benefits.conditions: The guidelines name waivers at universities; they do not say anything about fees at the preparatory institution.

benefits.limit_text: Economy-class air ticket to Japan, and an economy-class ticket home at the end of the scholarship
benefits.conditions: Outbound ticket from the international airport nearest the grantee's residence (in principle in the country of nationality), only if the grantee arrives in the specified period. A ticket via a third country is given if a visa must be collected there or there is no direct flight. The return ticket needs an application and is only for grantees who finish and go home by the end of the scholarship period; none if they leave early or stay on in Japan. Grantees pay for domestic travel to the home airport, airport taxes and fees, travel inside Japan, travel insurance and baggage costs.
Grantees may live in the preparatory institution's accommodation, a university residence hall for international students (limited rooms) or private housing; the grantee pays in each case.

benefits.limit_text: Grantees must join National Health Insurance on arrival
benefits.conditions: The guidelines do not say whether the scholarship pays the premiums. Travel insurance is the grantee's own cost.

requirements.text: Application Form on the FY2027 form, with a clear photograph taken within six months (4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper body, full face, no hat; name and nationality written on the back). All documents in Japanese or English, or with a translation in one of those. Submit two packets: a set of originals and a set of copies, and write the document number in the upper right corner of the first page of each.

Direct Placement Preference Form (FY2027 form): submitted only after passing the first screening, with a preferred university and department chosen from the list supplied by the Japanese mission. Ask the mission first about courses, places, language requirements, entrance exams and enrolment periods.
requirements.conditional_rule: only for applicants who choose Social Sciences and Humanities and are eligible for direct placement, or who want direct placement whatever their field

requirements.text: Academic transcripts for all school years of the school or university attended, showing the grade scale and the grades in all subjects, issued by the school or university or by the national government. Upper secondary school applicants submit the upper secondary transcript; applicants who attend or finished a university submit transcripts from both. Applicants still in school also submit a transcript at graduation by the time of enrolment.

Certificate of graduation (or certificate of prospective graduation if not yet graduated) from the school or university attended. Those at university also submit their upper secondary school certificate; university graduates submit both. A copy attested by an authorised official is acceptable, because documents are not returned.

Recommendation letter from a class teacher or the principal of the last school attended, in free format (a sample is available). Applicants still studying get it from the school or university they attend; graduates get it from the school or university they graduated from.
Medical certificate on the FY2027 form, completed and signed by a physician.

requirements.conditional_rule: only for those currently enrolled in a university

requirements.text: Certificate of a university entrance qualification exam. It may be submitted in place of the transcript, graduation certificate and recommendation letter.
requirements.conditional_rule: only for those who passed such an exam

requirements.text: Japanese or English proficiency certificate showing name and level or score: 2 copies, no original needed. Issue date no earlier than two years before the application date. Also fill in the language fields of the application form.
requirements.conditional_rule: only if the applicant has one

application_steps.title: Check the embassy call and prepare the FY2027 forms
application_steps.detail: Recruitment is run by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of your nationality, which decides the dates and details; the process and schedule differ by nationality. The call page says recruitment for April arrivals takes place in April to May of the year before, and first screening runs from May to August. Download the FY2027 application form and medical certificate, ask for a recommendation letter, and read the Application Guidelines.

application_steps.title: Choose field, course and up to three majors
application_steps.detail: Pick Social Sciences and Humanities or Natural Sciences, then a course (A or B, or A, B or C) and first, second and third choice majors. Art and music fields are not eligible. You may not change course after selection.

application_steps.title: Submit the application set to the Japanese mission
application_steps.detail: Hand in the full document set (originals and a set of copies) to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality by its deadline. Do not send documents to MEXT in Japan. Documents are not returned. Do not apply to any other MEXT programme at the same time.

application_steps.title: First screening at the Japanese mission
application_steps.detail: The mission checks documents, runs written academic exams for all applicants and holds interviews. Social Sciences and Humanities applicants sit Japanese (A), English (A) and Mathematics (A). Natural Sciences applicants sit Japanese (B), English (B) and Mathematics (B) plus Chemistry and Physics (Natural Sciences A) or Chemistry and Biology (Natural Sciences B and C). Calculators are not allowed. The mission announces the date of the results; reasons for results are not given, and passing does not guarantee a scholarship.

application_steps.title: Direct placement consultation, if you ask for it
application_steps.detail: After passing the first screening, eligible applicants (or those who want direct placement) submit the preference form. The university checks school grades and language ability, possibly with a language test score such as JLPT, an interview or other exams. Consultation runs from after the second screening until 12 February 2027; if no university agrees, you go through the preparatory institution.

application_steps.title: Second screening by MEXT and final result
application_steps.detail: The mission recommends applicants who passed the first screening to MEXT. MEXT carries out the second screening and chooses grantees from each course. The mission tells applicants the final result after February 2027, without reasons. Objections to the university placement are not accepted.

application_steps.title: Visa, arrival and preparatory year
application_steps.detail: Get a new Student visa at the Japanese mission in your country and arrive between 1 and 7 April 2027 (autumn-term direct placement: the period set by the university). Open a Japan Post Bank account and join National Health Insurance on arrival. The first year is normally the preparatory course (ABK College or Osaka University), after which you take the entrance exam of the university MEXT designates.

application_steps.title: Meet the conditions that keep the scholarship going
application_steps.detail: Payment is suspended or cancelled for false statements, breaking the pledge to MEXT, a sentence of detention over 1 year, school discipline, poor grades that make finishing on time impossible, not holding a Student visa, unapproved other scholarships, or moving to a higher level without approved extension; some or all payments may have to be repaid. Grantees are expected to join school and community activities and, after returning home, to keep in touch with the university and help the Japanese mission with surveys and events.

not_stated: Embassy deadlines, exam dates and result dates (set by each Japanese mission; the pages read give none)
List of participating universities (supplied by each Japanese mission for direct placement; MEXT chooses the university otherwise)
Minimum Japanese or English test scores (language certificate is optional)
Whether the scholarship pays National Health Insurance premiums
